r9_p_annotation: Per R9-P, the Big Hair Day (13 cells) and Balea MEN Styling Powder (2 cells) lane-error calls were owner questions (d), later settled by R8-Q1/R8-Q2. Round 8 is not a clean PASS under R3-L; the historical scoring values below are preserved.
method: TARGETED r8 re-check under R3-L/R4-L, LOCK-1-S, R6-Q1/R6-T and R7-F/R7-Q1/R7-Q2/R7-Q3; A=Claude Opus, B=Codex. Round-7 join, normalization and agreement method adapted. Raw disagreement counts are never altered by adjudication.

scope.denominator_explanation: Step 1 names the historical r7 denominator (69); both r8 lanes, cohort and scope audit contain 76 records. All 76 are scored; no arbitrary seven products are dropped.

normalisation: route is compared as {destination,state,boundary_reason}; boundary_reason is populated only for provisional_boundary. This retains evidence_gate, formula_conflict, mixed_promise, li_g0_provisional and pending_leave_in_addendum; committed and held are never folded together. Non-boundary pair/reason vocabulary remains calculation log.
application_moment compares primary only: {primary,also[]} versus string. also[] is excluded as requested. provides_heat_protection compares the boolean value, not research-trace wrappers.
buildup/alcohol notes: {fired:false}, not_fired and does_not_fire -> does_not_fire; {fired:true}, fired and fires -> fires. null remains null.

Set-valued arrays (secondary_jobs, mechanisms, review_triggers, flags) are deduplicated and sorted. Object keys are sorted for comparison. Free prose and rule-path order remain log differences, not behavioural defects.
neutral_fact folds whitespace, typographic quotation marks and case as round 4. Tail INCI folds case, whitespace and Parfum/Fragrance aliases; rank/status remain visible, T_S.alt is diagnostic-only.

Empty secondary_jobs/d8b_flags collections and null are equivalent only when no Styling profile exists (§4.7). Only explicitly informational_and_non_authoritative historical properties are masked. Any unmarked forbidden value remains scoreable.

confidence_internal is mapped to confidence; promise unknown/null -> not_assigned. Other lane-A-only fields are retained as schema-asymmetric calculation-log columns; missing is null. No user-facing disagreement is removed by adjudication.

lock_rules.quote: | R3-L | **Lock criterion „lanes agree" (PH1-11) means resolved, not identical.** Styling v1.0 may lock when every remaining A/B disagreement is resolved — either a lane error proven against a clear rule, or the rule gap behind it closed — **and** a final confirmation round shows only lane errors and no new rule gaps. Literal identity of both lanes on every value is not required. |

| R4-L | **Lock scope under R3-L: only differences in user-facing fields block the lock** — route/recommendability (incl. held vs committed, evidence gate), subtype, hold level, weight, finish, flexibility, target zone, application moment, primary and secondary jobs, heat protection, user-shown notes. Differences confined to the **calculation log** (reason code, rule path, internal review triggers, confidence, internal flags, lexicon placements that move no value) do not block: they are fixed in the text and documented, without a further round. Example: Bali Curls Sleek Stick — both lanes agree on every user field; only reason code and rule path differ. |

| LOCK-1-S | **LOCK-1 is SUSPENDED (Claude, 2026-10-13) until the items below are closed and confirmed.** The independent Claude-side review of `cf501908..HEAD` found that the r7 affected set missed products R6-T(3) reaches (screen used only „definiert"; missed „Definition"/„Define": Bali Gents Sea Salt Spray, Balea Leave-in Spray Sea Salt Care & Define — both lanes share the now-wrong `definition` secondary), and that r7 was never re-scored after the R7 fix (round-7/diff.js no longer runs at HEAD). The lock claim was premature. |

rules.quote: 1. the **job word of the confirmed product name**, when it names exactly one (Lockencreme ⇒ definition; Hitzeschutzspray ⇒ heat protection; Finishing-Spray / Glanzspray ⇒ finish). **A name with two or more job words does not decide; go to step 2** `[R1-H1]` (Elnett „Stylingspray Hitzeschutz 3 Tage Glatt" ⇒ pack front „Hitze Styling-Spray, glatt 3 Tage, starker Halt" ⇒ styling result, as PH1-14 rules). **Counting the name's job words `[RG2-21, RG2-5]`:** the product-type noun (Haarspray, Gel, Wachs, Puder, Schaumfestiger) names the job when it is the only job noun, and a shine or strength qualifier in the same name is not a second job (`schwarzkopf-taft-haarspray-glanz-halt-4` „Haarspray Glanz Halt 4" ⇒ one job, hold, so `hairspray`, as §5 says); name job words that name the same job count as one (Curl + Defining + Shaper on a curl product; „Glanz-Spray … Silky Shine"). **Which name words are job words `[RG3-1]`:** a **curl or wave word** in the product's own name (Locken-, Curl, Curls, Wellen-, Wave/Waves) is a curl job word `[R7-Q2]` — definition, or refresh when the product revives curls; a **salt noun** (Salzspray, Sea Salt Spray) names texture; a **product noun used as a form in a compound with another product noun** (Wax Spray, Spray Wax, Sprühwachs, Gel-Spray) names the form, not a job — go to step 2/3. Round-3 outcomes (historical, subject to the R7 amendment above): `bali-curls-volumizing-curl-spray-refreshing` („Volumizing Curl Spray": two job words ⇒ first C2 line, revival ⇒ held `refresher`); `wellaflex-schaumfestiger-locken-und-wellen-starker-halt` (name has hold + definition; the C1 phrase „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition` under R7-Q1 ⇒ 3.4 (iii)); `kevin-murphy-killer-curls` (two job words ⇒ the C2 hold line leads ⇒ primary `hold_fix`; the route stays D7 `curl_cream`, held); `jean-und-len-sea-salt-spray` (salt noun ⇒ texture); `redken-wax-spray` (Wax Spray names the form ⇒ first C2 line „Texturierendes Sprühwachs" ⇒ texture ⇒ `texture_spray`, §5). **Product noun vs qualifier, also inside a compound `[R4-Q7]`:** a product-type noun in the name (Wachs/Wax, Paste, Clay, Gel, Pomade, Fiber, Haarspray) names the job (molding or hold); a **shine or strength qualifier** in the name (Glanz, Glow, Shine, Strong, Power) is the finish or the grade, **never a second job — also inside a compound** (as „Haarspray Glanz"). Two product nouns of the same job count once. A **true job word** beside the product noun (Texture, Volume, Curl) makes two jobs ⇒ the name decides nothing ⇒ the lead line decides (step 2/3). The RG3-1 form compound stays for a product noun joined with a dispensing-form noun (Wax Spray, Sprühwachs, Gel-Spray: the spray is the form). Cases: `schwarzkopf-taft-gel-wax-glanz-halt-2` („Gel Wax Glanz": Gel and Wax name one job, Glanz is the finish) ⇒ `molding`, primary `hold_fix`, finish `glänzend`, and its D8b flag is kept internally (R4-Q7; §7.5); `got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay` („Styling Paste … Texture Clay": Paste/Clay + the job word Texture ⇒ two jobs) ⇒ the C2 line „… ultra krassem Halt" leads ⇒ primary `hold_fix`, `texture` secondary; `balea-haarwachs-glow-wax` (Glow is a qualifier) ⇒ `hold_fix`. **Look names and shine nouns `[R4-Q2]`:** „Beach Waves", „Strandwellen", „beachy" name the **salt-spray texture look** ⇒ `texture` (`li_function: no`), not curl definition; RG3-1's wave nouns cover curl/wave definition and revival products („Wellen-Spray", „Wellenauffrischer"), not beach-look names (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance` ⇒ texture ⇒ 3.4 (ii) ⇒ committed `salt_spray`). „Glaze", „Topcoat" and „Gloss" are shine job nouns (with the R2-Q3 list: Glanz, Shine, Gloss, Finish) ⇒ `syoss-glaze-topcoat` („Glaze Topcoat": one job, shine; R3-Q3 lets the one-job name win) ⇒ `styling_result` ⇒ 3.5 ⇒ committed `shine_finish`. Slogans in a name („Big Hair Day", „Salon Blow-Out") name no job and are skipped (RG2-17). **Shop-title fallback `[R3-Q2]`:** the confirmed name is the pack name (C1) or the brand's German-page name (C2). When **neither** shows the product name, the **product-type noun of the retailer's product title** (Hitzeschutzspray, Öl, Serum, Haarspray, Gel, Wachs …; dm „syoss **Hitzeschutzspray** Keratin") serves as the confirmed-name job word for this step and for D2 (§4.3 3.1), with review `name_from_retailer_title`, **provided the type noun agrees across the retailer titles captured `[R3-H4 (d)]`** — two titles with different type nouns (e.g. „Hitzeschutzspray" vs „Haarspray") give no fallback: the name decides nothing, the lead falls to steps 2–3, review `retailer_title_type_noun_conflict` (R1-H1's two-job-word rule covers two nouns in **one** name). **Every other word of a retailer title never counts** (R2-H1, the C3 rule): qualifiers, variant names, ingredient words and any second noun stay C3 traces. The real pack names of the products concerned are captured (29 confirmed names were retailer-title only in round 3, node, `round-3/diff.json` `packet_checks.confirmed_name_tier_C3`; P3-7, R3-T), and a captured pack or brand-page name replaces the fallback (the round-4 freeze replaces it from `capture/packnames-r7.json` wherever A3/A11 confirm a name, §4.6). Cases: `syoss-hitzeschutzspray-keratin-heat` ⇒ heat protection ⇒ 3.3 (§11.21); `loreal-elvital-haaroel-oel-magique-alle-haartypen`, `john-frieda-haarserum-frizz-ease-der-baendiger`, `garnier-fructis-sleek-and-stay-heat-activated-serum` ⇒ „Öl"/„Serum" ⇒ D2 by the letter (§4.6);

| Decision | Structured judgment: primary = the job the C1/C2 lead promise (§4.2 order) states; secondaries = up to two further jobs the C1/C2 claims state explicitly. **Primary `[RG-11]`:** the first **job-bearing** phrase of the lead promise; product nouns (Gel, Gelee, Paste, Wachs) and strength phrases („mit mittlerem Halt") are not job-bearing unless nothing else is; shaping/forming wording maps to `hold_fix`. **A strength phrase is not job-bearing when it qualifies a product noun or follows another job phrase („Gel mit mittlerem Halt"); when the hold is the lead's subject („Intensiver Halt für …", „Starker Halt –") the lead states `hold_fix` `[RG2-4]`** (`syoss-professional-performance-max-hold-power-wax`: „Intensiver Halt für glatte und glänzende … Looks" ⇒ `hold_fix`). **A curl/wave noun with a shaping or setting verb („Locken formen", „Curl Shaper", „Wellen über Nacht") states `definition`; shaping without a curl/wave noun stays `hold_fix` `[RG2-5]`** (`syoss-curl-cream-gel-3in1` „Locken zu formen und zu definieren" ⇒ `definition`). **Job vocabulary `[RG2-6, RG2-7; R6-T (3)]`:** Schwung, Sprungkraft, Spannkraft, Fülle ⇒ `volume`; **an adjective before a job phrase is not a separate job `[R7-Q1]`** (Wellaflex „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition`). (Elastizität is a flexibility word, §6.9, never a job); taming or smoothing flyaways, „abstehende Haare/Härchen" or „Babyhaare" ⇒ `frizz_control`; `sleek` only for a smooth or straight result of the whole style („glatte Looks", „Sleek-Look") (`john-frieda-frizz-ease-zauberformel-seiden-finish-creme` „Glättet abstehende Haare" ⇒ `frizz_control`). **Definition `[R6-T (3), R7-Q2]`: a curl/wave word in the product's own confirmed name supplies `definition` (with §4.2's Beach Waves texture and curl-revival refresh exceptions); in descriptive sentences an explicit promise to define or shape curls/waves is required. „Definition“/„Define“ for a non-curl look and a result phrase such as „definierter Look“ never supply `definition`** (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance`: no definition secondary). **Secondaries `[RG-12; RG2-16, ruled „open" by R2-T]`:** any job word of this vocabulary stated in a C1/C2 promise line — including the RG-12 mappings: a C1/C2 hold claim with a strength word ⇒ `hold_fix`; an anti-frizz/flyaway word ⇒ `frizz_control`; a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; **job words of the confirmed name count as secondaries** after the primary, in name order, **before** the claim lines (still at most two). **Formula gate** (property set §2.12): `hold_fix` ⇒ the D8b hold-mechanism set (§7.5); `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. A failing secondary is **dropped and recorded**; a failing primary is **kept** and tagged `job_formula_conflict` + review. **Order, gate and refill `[RG4-17]`** (closes RG2-16's „open"): list the eligible candidates in order — the confirmed name's job words first (after the primary, in name order), then the C1/C2 promise lines in packet order, each line's job words in text order — and take the first two; apply the formula gate; when the gate drops one, **refill from the next eligible candidate** (still at most two). **Humidity and duration lines never state a job; an explicit anti-frizz word in them does** („Schutz vor Frizz & Feuchtigkeit" ⇒ `frizz_control`; „hält bis zu 72 h" ⇒ none). **A fixing verb without a strength word** („fixiert die Frisur zuverlässig") **states `hold_fix` as a secondary and sets no level `[RG4-12]`** (`balea-overnight-wellenspray`). **A technology, formula or complex label is never a job `[RG4-10]`** („POWER-SHINE-TECHNOLOGIE" states no `shine`). **Brand line / collection names never supply any job `[R7-Q3]`** (Frizz Ease, Traumlocken, Volume Lift, Diamond Sleek, Glow & Shine, Nutricurls …); the product's own name words decide (§4.2). **Names `[R4-Q2, R4-Q7, R7-Q2]`:** „Glaze", „Topcoat", „Gloss" state `shine`; „Beach Waves" / „Strandwellen" / „beachy" state `texture`; a product noun states `hold_fix` (molding/hold) and its shine or strength qualifier states no second job; a true job word beside it (Texture, Volume, Curl) is a job word (`got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay`: primary `hold_fix` from the lead C2 line, secondary `texture` from the name) |

(Elastizität is a flexibility word, §6.9, never a job); taming or smoothing flyaways, „abstehende Haare/Härchen" or „Babyhaare" ⇒ `frizz_control`; `sleek` only for a smooth or straight result of the whole style („glatte Looks", „Sleek-Look") (`john-frieda-frizz-ease-zauberformel-seiden-finish-creme` „Glättet abstehende Haare" ⇒ `frizz_control`). **Definition `[R6-T (3), R7-Q2]`: a curl/wave word in the product's own confirmed name supplies `definition` (with §4.2's Beach Waves texture and curl-revival refresh exceptions); in descriptive sentences an explicit promise to define or shape curls/waves is required. „Definition“/„Define“ for a non-curl look and a result phrase such as „definierter Look“ never supply `definition`** (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance`: no definition secondary). **Secondaries `[RG-12; RG2-16, ruled „open" by R2-T]`:** any job word of this vocabulary stated in a C1/C2 promise line — including the RG-12 mappings: a C1/C2 hold claim with a strength word ⇒ `hold_fix`; an anti-frizz/flyaway word ⇒ `frizz_control`; a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; **job words of the confirmed name count as secondaries** after the primary, in name order, **before** the claim lines (still at most two). **Formula gate** (property set §2.12): `hold_fix` ⇒ the D8b hold-mechanism set (§7.5); `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. A failing secondary is **dropped and recorded**; a failing primary is **kept** and tagged `job_formula_conflict` + review. **Order, gate and refill `[RG4-17]`** (closes RG2-16's „open"): list the eligible candidates in order — the confirmed name's job words first (after the primary, in name order), then the C1/C2 promise lines in packet order, each line's job words in text order — and take the first two; apply the formula gate; when the gate drops one, **refill from the next eligible candidate** (still at most two). **Humidity and duration lines never state a job; an explicit anti-frizz word in them does** („Schutz vor Frizz & Feuchtigkeit" ⇒ `frizz_control`; „hält bis zu 72 h" ⇒ none). **A fixing verb without a strength word** („fixiert die Frisur zuverlässig") **states `hold_fix` as a secondary and sets no level `[RG4-12]`** (`balea-overnight-wellenspray`). **A technology, formula or complex label is never a job `[RG4-10]`** („POWER-SHINE-TECHNOLOGIE" states no `shine`). **Brand line / collection names never supply any job `[R7-Q3]`** (Frizz Ease, Traumlocken, Volume Lift, Diamond Sleek, Glow & Shine, Nutricurls …); the product's own name words decide (§4.2). **Names `[R4-Q2, R4-Q7, R7-Q2]`:** „Glaze", „Topcoat", „Gloss" state `shine`; „Beach Waves" / „Strandwellen" / „beachy" state `texture`; a product noun states `hold_fix` (molding/hold) and its shine or strength qualifier states no second job; a true job word beside it (Texture, Volume, Curl) is a job word (`got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay`: primary `hold_fix` from the lead C2 line, secondary `texture` from the name) |

rules.quote: 1. the **job word of the confirmed product name**, when it names exactly one (Lockencreme ⇒ definition; Hitzeschutzspray ⇒ heat protection; Finishing-Spray / Glanzspray ⇒ finish). **A name with two or more job words does not decide; go to step 2** `[R1-H1]` (Elnett „Stylingspray Hitzeschutz 3 Tage Glatt" ⇒ pack front „Hitze Styling-Spray, glatt 3 Tage, starker Halt" ⇒ styling result, as PH1-14 rules). **Counting the name's job words `[RG2-21, RG2-5]`:** the product-type noun (Haarspray, Gel, Wachs, Puder, Schaumfestiger) names the job when it is the only job noun, and a shine or strength qualifier in the same name is not a second job (`schwarzkopf-taft-haarspray-glanz-halt-4` „Haarspray Glanz Halt 4" ⇒ one job, hold, so `hairspray`, as §5 says); name job words that name the same job count as one (Curl + Defining + Shaper on a curl product; „Glanz-Spray … Silky Shine"). **Which name words are job words `[RG3-1]`:** a **curl or wave word** in the product's own name (Locken-, Curl, Curls, Wellen-, Wave/Waves) is a curl job word `[R7-Q2]` — definition, or refresh when the product revives curls; a **salt noun** (Salzspray, Sea Salt Spray) names texture; a **product noun used as a form in a compound with another product noun** (Wax Spray, Spray Wax, Sprühwachs, Gel-Spray) names the form, not a job — go to step 2/3. Round-3 outcomes (historical, subject to the R7 amendment above): `bali-curls-volumizing-curl-spray-refreshing` („Volumizing Curl Spray": two job words ⇒ first C2 line, revival ⇒ held `refresher`); `wellaflex-schaumfestiger-locken-und-wellen-starker-halt` (name has hold + definition; the C1 phrase „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition` under R7-Q1 ⇒ 3.4 (iii)); `kevin-murphy-killer-curls` (two job words ⇒ the C2 hold line leads ⇒ primary `hold_fix`; the route stays D7 `curl_cream`, held); `jean-und-len-sea-salt-spray` (salt noun ⇒ texture); `redken-wax-spray` (Wax Spray names the form ⇒ first C2 line „Texturierendes Sprühwachs" ⇒ texture ⇒ `texture_spray`, §5). **Product noun vs qualifier, also inside a compound `[R4-Q7]`:** a product-type noun in the name (Wachs/Wax, Paste, Clay, Gel, Pomade, Fiber, Haarspray) names the job (molding or hold); a **shine or strength qualifier** in the name (Glanz, Glow, Shine, Strong, Power) is the finish or the grade, **never a second job — also inside a compound** (as „Haarspray Glanz"). Two product nouns of the same job count once. A **true job word** beside the product noun (Texture, Volume, Curl) makes two jobs ⇒ the name decides nothing ⇒ the lead line decides (step 2/3). The RG3-1 form compound stays for a product noun joined with a dispensing-form noun (Wax Spray, Sprühwachs, Gel-Spray: the spray is the form). Cases: `schwarzkopf-taft-gel-wax-glanz-halt-2` („Gel Wax Glanz": Gel and Wax name one job, Glanz is the finish) ⇒ `molding`, primary `hold_fix`, finish `glänzend`, and its D8b flag is kept internally (R4-Q7; §7.5); `got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay` („Styling Paste … Texture Clay": Paste/Clay + the job word Texture ⇒ two jobs) ⇒ the C2 line „… ultra krassem Halt" leads ⇒ primary `hold_fix`, `texture` secondary; `balea-haarwachs-glow-wax` (Glow is a qualifier) ⇒ `hold_fix`. **Look names and shine nouns `[R4-Q2]`:** „Beach Waves", „Strandwellen", „beachy" name the **salt-spray texture look** ⇒ `texture` (`li_function: no`), not curl definition; RG3-1's wave nouns cover curl/wave definition and revival products („Wellen-Spray", „Wellenauffrischer"), not beach-look names (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance` ⇒ texture ⇒ 3.4 (ii) ⇒ committed `salt_spray`). „Glaze", „Topcoat" and „Gloss" are shine job nouns (with the R2-Q3 list: Glanz, Shine, Gloss, Finish) ⇒ `syoss-glaze-topcoat` („Glaze Topcoat": one job, shine; R3-Q3 lets the one-job name win) ⇒ `styling_result` ⇒ 3.5 ⇒ committed `shine_finish`. Slogans in a name („Big Hair Day", „Salon Blow-Out") name no job and are skipped (RG2-17). **Shop-title fallback `[R3-Q2]`:** the confirmed name is the pack name (C1) or the brand's German-page name (C2). When **neither** shows the product name, the **product-type noun of the retailer's product title** (Hitzeschutzspray, Öl, Serum, Haarspray, Gel, Wachs …; dm „syoss **Hitzeschutzspray** Keratin") serves as the confirmed-name job word for this step and for D2 (§4.3 3.1), with review `name_from_retailer_title`, **provided the type noun agrees across the retailer titles captured `[R3-H4 (d)]`** — two titles with different type nouns (e.g. „Hitzeschutzspray" vs „Haarspray") give no fallback: the name decides nothing, the lead falls to steps 2–3, review `retailer_title_type_noun_conflict` (R1-H1's two-job-word rule covers two nouns in **one** name). **Every other word of a retailer title never counts** (R2-H1, the C3 rule): qualifiers, variant names, ingredient words and any second noun stay C3 traces. The real pack names of the products concerned are captured (29 confirmed names were retailer-title only in round 3, node, `round-3/diff.json` `packet_checks.confirmed_name_tier_C3`; P3-7, R3-T), and a captured pack or brand-page name replaces the fallback (the round-4 freeze replaces it from `capture/packnames-r7.json` wherever A3/A11 confirm a name, §4.6). rules.matched_fragment: a paste, wax, cream or powder worked into dry hair by hand is `dry_restyle`
rules.quote: | Decision | Transcription against the property-set anchors (§2.13), from the verbatim directions (any G1 tier; not claim-gated). **Reading the two damp anchors `[operational — property set §2.13 anchor text]`:** `before_heat` when the directions make a heat step a **required** next step (blow-dry or iron named, no air-dry option) or apply to dry hair before a hot tool; `damp_before_drying` when air-drying is allowed, drying is unspecified, or blow-drying is offered as optional („für optimales Ergebnis föhnen"). This resolves property set §9 item 4: `alcina-foehn-lotion` and `balea-foehnlotion-volume-effect` both read `before_heat` if their directions require the blow-dry. `second_day` only when the **directions** lead with refreshing between washes — marketing copy („ideal zum Auffrischen") is not directions. **Spray-only directions `[RG-2]`:** directions that consist only of spraying the product onto the hair (distance, evenness, optional targeting of strands — „Aus 30 cm Abstand sprühen") with no moisture state, no drying or heat step and no shaping step read **`dry_finish`** (the product is applied last, onto the finished style), confidence `moderate`; missing or copied directions stay `unresolved`. **Equal alternatives `[RG-8]`:** when the directions offer two moments as equal options („in handtuchtrockenes oder trockenes Haar", „feucht oder trocken"), the **first-named** is primary and the others go to `also[]`. **`dry_restyle` needs a named shaping act `[RG2-8]`** (kneten, einkneten, formen, stylen, in Form bringen, toupieren; **also einarbeiten, durcharbeiten, mit den Fingern verteilen und formen `[RG3-7]`**; and **a paste, wax, cream or powder worked into dry hair by hand is `dry_restyle` `[RG3-7]`** — `got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay` „zwischen deinen Handflächen [verreiben] und … ins trockene Haar ein[arbeiten]", `osis-dust-it` „mit den Fingern in das trockene Haar einarbeiten", `syoss-professional-performance-max-hold-power-wax` „in den Handflächen verreiben … Auf trockenem Haar anwenden"): spraying or distributing on dry hair without one is `dry_finish`; a product sprayed strand by strand to revive curls is `dry_finish` (`alverde-locken-refresh-spray`), while a named shaping act such as „und nach Wunsch stylen" or „einkneten" makes it `dry_restyle` (`redken-refreshing-curl-mist` „sprühen und sanft einkneten" ⇒ `dry_restyle`). **Shaping with no moisture state `[RG2-9]`** (mirror of RG-2): directions that name a shaping step but no moisture state, no drying and no heat step read **`dry_restyle`**, confidence `moderate` (`redken-powder-grip-03` „über das Haar streuen … mit den Fingern durch das Haar kneten"; `redken-root-tease`; `got2b-kleber-4-brows-and-edges-2in1-stylinggel`); missing or copied directions stay `unresolved`. **Stroking over dry hair without a shaping act `[RG4-14]`** (a stick passed over the finished style to lay down flyaways) is `dry_finish` (`balea-styling-finishing-stick` „Nach dem Frisurenstyling sanft über die abstehenden Härchen streichen") |

Round-3 outcomes (historical, subject to the R7 amendment above): `bali-curls-volumizing-curl-spray-refreshing` („Volumizing Curl Spray": two job words ⇒ first C2 line, revival ⇒ held `refresher`); `wellaflex-schaumfestiger-locken-und-wellen-starker-halt` (name has hold + definition; the C1 phrase „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition` under R7-Q1 ⇒ 3.4 (iii)); `kevin-murphy-killer-curls` (two job words ⇒ the C2 hold line leads ⇒ primary `hold_fix`; the route stays D7 `curl_cream`, held); `jean-und-len-sea-salt-spray` (salt noun ⇒ texture); `redken-wax-spray` (Wax Spray names the form ⇒ first C2 line „Texturierendes Sprühwachs" ⇒ texture ⇒ `texture_spray`, §5). **Product noun vs qualifier, also inside a compound `[R4-Q7]`:** a product-type noun in the name (Wachs/Wax, Paste, Clay, Gel, Pomade, Fiber, Haarspray) names the job (molding or hold); a **shine or strength qualifier** in the name (Glanz, Glow, Shine, Strong, Power) is the finish or the grade, **never a second job — also inside a compound** (as „Haarspray Glanz"). Two product nouns of the same job count once. A **true job word** beside the product noun (Texture, Volume, Curl) makes two jobs ⇒ the name decides nothing ⇒ the lead line decides (step 2/3). The RG3-1 form compound stays for a product noun joined with a dispensing-form noun (Wax Spray, Sprühwachs, Gel-Spray: the spray is the form). Cases: `schwarzkopf-taft-gel-wax-glanz-halt-2` („Gel Wax Glanz": Gel and Wax name one job, Glanz is the finish) ⇒ `molding`, primary `hold_fix`, finish `glänzend`, and its D8b flag is kept internally (R4-Q7; §7.5); `got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay` („Styling Paste … Texture Clay": Paste/Clay + the job word Texture ⇒ two jobs) ⇒ the C2 line „… ultra krassem Halt" leads ⇒ primary `hold_fix`, `texture` secondary; `balea-haarwachs-glow-wax` (Glow is a qualifier) ⇒ `hold_fix`. **Look names and shine nouns `[R4-Q2]`:** „Beach Waves", „Strandwellen", „beachy" name the **salt-spray texture look** ⇒ `texture` (`li_function: no`), not curl definition; RG3-1's wave nouns cover curl/wave definition and revival products („Wellen-Spray", „Wellenauffrischer"), not beach-look names (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance` ⇒ texture ⇒ 3.4 (ii) ⇒ committed `salt_spray`). „Glaze", „Topcoat" and „Gloss" are shine job nouns (with the R2-Q3 list: Glanz, Shine, Gloss, Finish) ⇒ `syoss-glaze-topcoat` („Glaze Topcoat": one job, shine; R3-Q3 lets the one-job name win) ⇒ `styling_result` ⇒ 3.5 ⇒ committed `shine_finish`. Slogans in a name („Big Hair Day", „Salon Blow-Out") name no job and are skipped (RG2-17). **Shop-title fallback `[R3-Q2]`:** the confirmed name is the pack name (C1) or the brand's German-page name (C2). When **neither** shows the product name, the **product-type noun of the retailer's product title** (Hitzeschutzspray, Öl, Serum, Haarspray, Gel, Wachs …; dm „syoss **Hitzeschutzspray** Keratin") serves as the confirmed-name job word for this step and for D2 (§4.3 3.1), with review `name_from_retailer_title`, **provided the type noun agrees across the retailer titles captured `[R3-H4 (d)]`** — two titles with different type nouns (e.g. „Hitzeschutzspray" vs „Haarspray") give no fallback: the name decides nothing, the lead falls to steps 2–3, review `retailer_title_type_noun_conflict` (R1-H1's two-job-word rule covers two nouns in **one** name). **Every other word of a retailer title never counts** (R2-H1, the C3 rule): qualifiers, variant names, ingredient words and any second noun stay C3 traces. The real pack names of the products concerned are captured (29 confirmed names were retailer-title only in round 3, node, `round-3/diff.json` `packet_checks.confirmed_name_tier_C3`; P3-7, R3-T), and a captured pack or brand-page name replaces the fallback (the round-4 freeze replaces it from `capture/packnames-r7.json` wherever A3/A11 confirm a name, §4.6). Cases: `syoss-hitzeschutzspray-keratin-heat` ⇒ heat protection ⇒ 3.3 (§11.21); `loreal-elvital-haaroel-oel-magique-alle-haartypen`, `john-frieda-haarserum-frizz-ease-der-baendiger`, `garnier-fructis-sleek-and-stay-heat-activated-serum` ⇒ „Öl"/„Serum" ⇒ D2 by the letter (§4.6);

rules.quote: **A line with no job word is skipped `[RG2-17, R7-F]`:** at steps 2 and 3, a lead line that states no job word („Haarwachs-Stift für trendige Styles", „Praktische Anwendung") is passed over and the next C1/C2 line with a job word is the lead (`balea-haarwachs-styling-stick`, sealed round-2 slot 2: past „Haarwachs-Stift für trendige Styles" and „Praktische Anwendung" to „Für ein glattes & glänzendes Finish", the reading both lanes took in round 2 ⇒ `shine_finish`). **The name step comes first `[R2-H3]`:** RG2-17 applies only at steps 2 and 3; when the confirmed name names exactly one job (step 1, RG2-21), the name decides and later lines with a more specific job word are secondaries. `balea-haarwachs-styling-stick` (pack name „Styling WAX STICK", dm title „Haarwachs Styling Stick": one product-type noun, Wachs/Wax) ⇒ lead = molding ⇒ **`molding`**, not `shine_finish`; „glattes, glänzendes Finish", „Ideal für den Sleek-Look" and „auch gegen Babyhaare" are secondary jobs and uses (§4.6, §11.16).

rules.quote: | Decision | Structured judgment: primary = the job the C1/C2 lead promise (§4.2 order) states; secondaries = up to two further jobs the C1/C2 claims state explicitly. **Primary `[RG-11]`:** the first **job-bearing** phrase of the lead promise; product nouns (Gel, Gelee, Paste, Wachs) and strength phrases („mit mittlerem Halt") are not job-bearing unless nothing else is; shaping/forming wording maps to `hold_fix`. **A strength phrase is not job-bearing when it qualifies a product noun or follows another job phrase („Gel mit mittlerem Halt"); when the hold is the lead's subject („Intensiver Halt für …", „Starker Halt –") the lead states `hold_fix` `[RG2-4]`** (`syoss-professional-performance-max-hold-power-wax`: „Intensiver Halt für glatte und glänzende … Looks" ⇒ `hold_fix`). **A curl/wave noun with a shaping or setting verb („Locken formen", „Curl Shaper", „Wellen über Nacht") states `definition`; shaping without a curl/wave noun stays `hold_fix` `[RG2-5]`** (`syoss-curl-cream-gel-3in1` „Locken zu formen und zu definieren" ⇒ `definition`). **Job vocabulary `[RG2-6, RG2-7; R6-T (3)]`:** Schwung, Sprungkraft, Spannkraft, Fülle ⇒ `volume`; **an adjective before a job phrase is not a separate job `[R7-Q1]`** (Wellaflex „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition`). (Elastizität is a flexibility word, §6.9, never a job); taming or smoothing flyaways, „abstehende Haare/Härchen" or „Babyhaare" ⇒ `frizz_control`; `sleek` only for a smooth or straight result of the whole style („glatte Looks", „Sleek-Look") (`john-frieda-frizz-ease-zauberformel-seiden-finish-creme` „Glättet abstehende Haare" ⇒ `frizz_control`). **Definition `[R6-T (3), R7-Q2]`: a curl/wave word in the product's own confirmed name supplies `definition` (with §4.2's Beach Waves texture and curl-revival refresh exceptions); in descriptive sentences an explicit promise to define or shape curls/waves is required. „Definition“/„Define“ for a non-curl look and a result phrase such as „definierter Look“ never supply `definition`** (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance`: no definition secondary). **Secondaries `[RG-12; RG2-16, ruled „open" by R2-T]`:** any job word of this vocabulary stated in a C1/C2 promise line — including the RG-12 mappings: a C1/C2 hold claim with a strength word ⇒ `hold_fix`; an anti-frizz/flyaway word ⇒ `frizz_control`; a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; **job words of the confirmed name count as secondaries** after the primary, in name order, **before** the claim lines (still at most two). **Formula gate** (property set §2.12): `hold_fix` ⇒ the D8b hold-mechanism set (§7.5); `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. A failing secondary is **dropped and recorded**; a failing primary is **kept** and tagged `job_formula_conflict` + review. **Order, gate and refill `[RG4-17]`** (closes RG2-16's „open"): list the eligible candidates in order — the confirmed name's job words first (after the primary, in name order), then the C1/C2 promise lines in packet order, each line's job words in text order — and take the first two; apply the formula gate; when the gate drops one, **refill from the next eligible candidate** (still at most two). **Humidity and duration lines never state a job; an explicit anti-frizz word in them does** („Schutz vor Frizz & Feuchtigkeit" ⇒ `frizz_control`; „hält bis zu 72 h" ⇒ none). **A fixing verb without a strength word** („fixiert die Frisur zuverlässig") **states `hold_fix` as a secondary and sets no level `[RG4-12]`** (`balea-overnight-wellenspray`). **A technology, formula or complex label is never a job `[RG4-10]`** („POWER-SHINE-TECHNOLOGIE" states no `shine`). **Brand line / collection names never supply any job `[R7-Q3]`** (Frizz Ease, Traumlocken, Volume Lift, Diamond Sleek, Glow & Shine, Nutricurls …); the product's own name words decide (§4.2). **Names `[R4-Q2, R4-Q7, R7-Q2]`:** „Glaze", „Topcoat", „Gloss" state `shine`; „Beach Waves" / „Strandwellen" / „beachy" state `texture`; a product noun states `hold_fix` (molding/hold) and its shine or strength qualifier states no second job; a true job word beside it (Texture, Volume, Curl) is a job word (`got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay`: primary `hold_fix` from the lead C2 line, secondary `texture` from the name) |

The one-job confirmed name leads before C2 sentences. Thus A shine is primary and Glättet abstehende Haare/bändigt Frizz supplies frizz_control secondary, passing wax_lipid/silicone_coat. Für sofortiges Volumen und einen langanhaltenden Frische-Effekt sorgt das Elvital Collagen Lifter Big Hair Day Erfrischendes Volumenspray von L'ORÉAL PARiS. Dank der innovativen Tri-Düse lässt sich das Spray gezielt am Haaransatz anwenden, um diesen in Sekundenschnelle anzuheben. rules.quote: | Decision | Structured judgment: primary = the job the C1/C2 lead promise (§4.2 order) states; secondaries = up to two further jobs the C1/C2 claims state explicitly. **Primary `[RG-11]`:** the first **job-bearing** phrase of the lead promise; product nouns (Gel, Gelee, Paste, Wachs) and strength phrases („mit mittlerem Halt") are not job-bearing unless nothing else is; shaping/forming wording maps to `hold_fix`. **A strength phrase is not job-bearing when it qualifies a product noun or follows another job phrase („Gel mit mittlerem Halt"); when the hold is the lead's subject („Intensiver Halt für …", „Starker Halt –") the lead states `hold_fix` `[RG2-4]`** (`syoss-professional-performance-max-hold-power-wax`: „Intensiver Halt für glatte und glänzende … Looks" ⇒ `hold_fix`). **A curl/wave noun with a shaping or setting verb („Locken formen", „Curl Shaper", „Wellen über Nacht") states `definition`; shaping without a curl/wave noun stays `hold_fix` `[RG2-5]`** (`syoss-curl-cream-gel-3in1` „Locken zu formen und zu definieren" ⇒ `definition`). **Job vocabulary `[RG2-6, RG2-7; R6-T (3)]`:** Schwung, Sprungkraft, Spannkraft, Fülle ⇒ `volume`; **an adjective before a job phrase is not a separate job `[R7-Q1]`** (Wellaflex „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition`). (Elastizität is a flexibility word, §6.9, never a job); taming or smoothing flyaways, „abstehende Haare/Härchen" or „Babyhaare" ⇒ `frizz_control`; `sleek` only for a smooth or straight result of the whole style („glatte Looks", „Sleek-Look") (`john-frieda-frizz-ease-zauberformel-seiden-finish-creme` „Glättet abstehende Haare" ⇒ `frizz_control`). **Definition `[R6-T (3), R7-Q2]`: a curl/wave word in the product's own confirmed name supplies `definition` (with §4.2's Beach Waves texture and curl-revival refresh exceptions); in descriptive sentences an explicit promise to define or shape curls/waves is required. „Definition“/„Define“ for a non-curl look and a result phrase such as „definierter Look“ never supply `definition`** (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance`: no definition secondary). **Secondaries `[RG-12; RG2-16, ruled „open" by R2-T]`:** any job word of this vocabulary stated in a C1/C2 promise line — including the RG-12 mappings: a C1/C2 hold claim with a strength word ⇒ `hold_fix`; an anti-frizz/flyaway word ⇒ `frizz_control`; a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; **job words of the confirmed name count as secondaries** after the primary, in name order, **before** the claim lines (still at most two). **Formula gate** (property set §2.12): `hold_fix` ⇒ the D8b hold-mechanism set (§7.5); `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. A failing secondary is **dropped and recorded**; a failing primary is **kept** and tagged `job_formula_conflict` + review. **Order, gate and refill `[RG4-17]`** (closes RG2-16's „open"): list the eligible candidates in order — the confirmed name's job words first (after the primary, in name order), then the C1/C2 promise lines in packet order, each line's job words in text order — and take the first two; apply the formula gate; when the gate drops one, **refill from the next eligible candidate** (still at most two). **Humidity and duration lines never state a job; an explicit anti-frizz word in them does** („Schutz vor Frizz & Feuchtigkeit" ⇒ `frizz_control`; „hält bis zu 72 h" ⇒ none). **A fixing verb without a strength word** („fixiert die Frisur zuverlässig") **states `hold_fix` as a secondary and sets no level `[RG4-12]`** (`balea-overnight-wellenspray`). **A technology, formula or complex label is never a job `[RG4-10]`** („POWER-SHINE-TECHNOLOGIE" states no `shine`). **Brand line / collection names never supply any job `[R7-Q3]`** (Frizz Ease, Traumlocken, Volume Lift, Diamond Sleek, Glow & Shine, Nutricurls …); the product's own name words decide (§4.2). **Names `[R4-Q2, R4-Q7, R7-Q2]`:** „Glaze", „Topcoat", „Gloss" state `shine`; „Beach Waves" / „Strandwellen" / „beachy" state `texture`; a product noun states `hold_fix` (molding/hold) and its shine or strength qualifier states no second job; a true job word beside it (Texture, Volume, Curl) is a job word (`got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay`: primary `hold_fix` from the lead C2 line, secondary `texture` from the name) |

Dann einfach … trocken föhnen") — is a usage step for `application_moment` and gives **`no`** (`balea-styling-spray-ultra-volumen`, `jean-und-len-sea-salt-spray`, `balea-sea-salt-texture-spray`). `no` also when directions give heat no role; `unresolved` when activation appears only at C3/C5 (`color-wow-dream-coat-supernatural-spray`, Douglas „wärmeaktiviertes Polymer"). A C1/C2 activation statement (in a claim or in the confirmed name) raises `no` to `yes` (property set §7 crossing 1). **The record carries the raised value, and the lanes apply the raise themselves `[RG4-18]`:** a lane sees the claims packet as well as the F/U directions, so it emits the final value — C1/C2 activation ⇒ `yes`; activation only at C3/C5 ⇒ `unresolved` (`guhl-foehn-spray-langzeit-volumen`: directions „Vor dem Föhnen aufsprühen" alone ⇒ `no`, the confirmed-name word „Föhn-Aktiv" ⇒ **`yes`**; `kms-thermashape-2-in-1-spray` „Hitzereaktives Spray" and `kms-thermashape-straightening-creme` „WÄRME-AKTIVIERUNG" ⇒ `yes`; `color-wow-dream-coat-supernatural-spray` ⇒ `unresolved`). *Superseded:* RG2-26's „in the blind round `heat_activated` reads the F/U directions only; name and claim activation raise it after unblinding" (round-4 lane A followed it and lane B did not, E4-2 and RG4-18; under v0.5 lane B's value is the record value). **Never heat protection** (§6.7).

rules.matched_fragment: the first **job-bearing** phrase of the lead promise
rules.quote: | Decision | Structured judgment: primary = the job the C1/C2 lead promise (§4.2 order) states; secondaries = up to two further jobs the C1/C2 claims state explicitly. **Primary `[RG-11]`:** the first **job-bearing** phrase of the lead promise; product nouns (Gel, Gelee, Paste, Wachs) and strength phrases („mit mittlerem Halt") are not job-bearing unless nothing else is; shaping/forming wording maps to `hold_fix`. **A strength phrase is not job-bearing when it qualifies a product noun or follows another job phrase („Gel mit mittlerem Halt"); when the hold is the lead's subject („Intensiver Halt für …", „Starker Halt –") the lead states `hold_fix` `[RG2-4]`** (`syoss-professional-performance-max-hold-power-wax`: „Intensiver Halt für glatte und glänzende … Looks" ⇒ `hold_fix`). **A curl/wave noun with a shaping or setting verb („Locken formen", „Curl Shaper", „Wellen über Nacht") states `definition`; shaping without a curl/wave noun stays `hold_fix` `[RG2-5]`** (`syoss-curl-cream-gel-3in1` „Locken zu formen und zu definieren" ⇒ `definition`). **Job vocabulary `[RG2-6, RG2-7; R6-T (3)]`:** Schwung, Sprungkraft, Spannkraft, Fülle ⇒ `volume`; **an adjective before a job phrase is not a separate job `[R7-Q1]`** (Wellaflex „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition`). (Elastizität is a flexibility word, §6.9, never a job); taming or smoothing flyaways, „abstehende Haare/Härchen" or „Babyhaare" ⇒ `frizz_control`; `sleek` only for a smooth or straight result of the whole style („glatte Looks", „Sleek-Look") (`john-frieda-frizz-ease-zauberformel-seiden-finish-creme` „Glättet abstehende Haare" ⇒ `frizz_control`). **Definition `[R6-T (3), R7-Q2]`: a curl/wave word in the product's own confirmed name supplies `definition` (with §4.2's Beach Waves texture and curl-revival refresh exceptions); in descriptive sentences an explicit promise to define or shape curls/waves is required. „Definition“/„Define“ for a non-curl look and a result phrase such as „definierter Look“ never supply `definition`** (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance`: no definition secondary). **Secondaries `[RG-12; RG2-16, ruled „open" by R2-T]`:** any job word of this vocabulary stated in a C1/C2 promise line — including the RG-12 mappings: a C1/C2 hold claim with a strength word ⇒ `hold_fix`; an anti-frizz/flyaway word ⇒ `frizz_control`; a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; **job words of the confirmed name count as secondaries** after the primary, in name order, **before** the claim lines (still at most two). **Formula gate** (property set §2.12): `hold_fix` ⇒ the D8b hold-mechanism set (§7.5); `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. A failing secondary is **dropped and recorded**; a failing primary is **kept** and tagged `job_formula_conflict` + review. **Order, gate and refill `[RG4-17]`** (closes RG2-16's „open"): list the eligible candidates in order — the confirmed name's job words first (after the primary, in name order), then the C1/C2 promise lines in packet order, each line's job words in text order — and take the first two; apply the formula gate; when the gate drops one, **refill from the next eligible candidate** (still at most two). **Humidity and duration lines never state a job; an explicit anti-frizz word in them does** („Schutz vor Frizz & Feuchtigkeit" ⇒ `frizz_control`; „hält bis zu 72 h" ⇒ none). **A fixing verb without a strength word** („fixiert die Frisur zuverlässig") **states `hold_fix` as a secondary and sets no level `[RG4-12]`** (`balea-overnight-wellenspray`). **A technology, formula or complex label is never a job `[RG4-10]`** („POWER-SHINE-TECHNOLOGIE" states no `shine`). **Brand line / collection names never supply any job `[R7-Q3]`** (Frizz Ease, Traumlocken, Volume Lift, Diamond Sleek, Glow & Shine, Nutricurls …); the product's own name words decide (§4.2). **Names `[R4-Q2, R4-Q7, R7-Q2]`:** „Glaze", „Topcoat", „Gloss" state `shine`; „Beach Waves" / „Strandwellen" / „beachy" state `texture`; a product noun states `hold_fix` (molding/hold) and its shine or strength qualifier states no second job; a true job word beside it (Texture, Volume, Curl) is a job word (`got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay`: primary `hold_fix` from the lead C2 line, secondary `texture` from the name) |

disagreements.explanation: R7-Q1 is written as a general adjective-before-job-phrase rule, not a Wellaflex-only exception. In the C2 lead intensiv glänzenden qualifies the following glatten Glass Hair-Effekt job phrase; it does not supply a separate earlier shine job. The smooth whole-style result supplies sleek; reduziert Frizz supplies the eligible frizz_control secondary via silicone_coat. Shine remains finish evidence under §6.8. B repeats the superseded pre-R7 separate-adjective job reading; A applies the governing amendment.

claims.text: Das Balea MEN Styling Powder verleiht dem Haar Volumen und einen matten Effekt. Es sorgt für extra Fülle und Textur, ideal für ein perfektes Ansatzvolumen und voluminöse Looks. Die leichte Formel hinterlässt ein mattes Finish ohne sichtbare Rückstände und beschwert das Haar nicht. Für ein individuelles und flexibles Styling kann das Styling Powder einfach im trockenen Haar verteilt und nach Wunsch modelliert werden.

rules.quote: 1. the **job word of the confirmed product name**, when it names exactly one (Lockencreme ⇒ definition; Hitzeschutzspray ⇒ heat protection; Finishing-Spray / Glanzspray ⇒ finish). **A name with two or more job words does not decide; go to step 2** `[R1-H1]` (Elnett „Stylingspray Hitzeschutz 3 Tage Glatt" ⇒ pack front „Hitze Styling-Spray, glatt 3 Tage, starker Halt" ⇒ styling result, as PH1-14 rules). **Counting the name's job words `[RG2-21, RG2-5]`:** the product-type noun (Haarspray, Gel, Wachs, Puder, Schaumfestiger) names the job when it is the only job noun, and a shine or strength qualifier in the same name is not a second job (`schwarzkopf-taft-haarspray-glanz-halt-4` „Haarspray Glanz Halt 4" ⇒ one job, hold, so `hairspray`, as §5 says); name job words that name the same job count as one (Curl + Defining + Shaper on a curl product; „Glanz-Spray … Silky Shine"). **Which name words are job words `[RG3-1]`:** a **curl or wave word** in the product's own name (Locken-, Curl, Curls, Wellen-, Wave/Waves) is a curl job word `[R7-Q2]` — definition, or refresh when the product revives curls; a **salt noun** (Salzspray, Sea Salt Spray) names texture; a **product noun used as a form in a compound with another product noun** (Wax Spray, Spray Wax, Sprühwachs, Gel-Spray) names the form, not a job — go to step 2/3. Round-3 outcomes (historical, subject to the R7 amendment above): `bali-curls-volumizing-curl-spray-refreshing` („Volumizing Curl Spray": two job words ⇒ first C2 line, revival ⇒ held `refresher`); `wellaflex-schaumfestiger-locken-und-wellen-starker-halt` (name has hold + definition; the C1 phrase „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition` under R7-Q1 ⇒ 3.4 (iii)); `kevin-murphy-killer-curls` (two job words ⇒ the C2 hold line leads ⇒ primary `hold_fix`; the route stays D7 `curl_cream`, held); `jean-und-len-sea-salt-spray` (salt noun ⇒ texture); `redken-wax-spray` (Wax Spray names the form ⇒ first C2 line „Texturierendes Sprühwachs" ⇒ texture ⇒ `texture_spray`, §5). **Product noun vs qualifier, also inside a compound `[R4-Q7]`:** a product-type noun in the name (Wachs/Wax, Paste, Clay, Gel, Pomade, Fiber, Haarspray) names the job (molding or hold); a **shine or strength qualifier** in the name (Glanz, Glow, Shine, Strong, Power) is the finish or the grade, **never a second job — also inside a compound** (as „Haarspray Glanz"). Two product nouns of the same job count once. A **true job word** beside the product noun (Texture, Volume, Curl) makes two jobs ⇒ the name decides nothing ⇒ the lead line decides (step 2/3). The RG3-1 form compound stays for a product noun joined with a dispensing-form noun (Wax Spray, Sprühwachs, Gel-Spray: the spray is the form). Cases: `schwarzkopf-taft-gel-wax-glanz-halt-2` („Gel Wax Glanz": Gel and Wax name one job, Glanz is the finish) ⇒ `molding`, primary `hold_fix`, finish `glänzend`, and its D8b flag is kept internally (R4-Q7; §7.5); `got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay` („Styling Paste … Texture Clay": Paste/Clay + the job word Texture ⇒ two jobs) ⇒ the C2 line „… ultra krassem Halt" leads ⇒ primary `hold_fix`, `texture` secondary; `balea-haarwachs-glow-wax` (Glow is a qualifier) ⇒ `hold_fix`. **Look names and shine nouns `[R4-Q2]`:** „Beach Waves", „Strandwellen", „beachy" name the **salt-spray texture look** ⇒ `texture` (`li_function: no`), not curl definition; RG3-1's wave nouns cover curl/wave definition and revival products („Wellen-Spray", „Wellenauffrischer"), not beach-look names (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance` ⇒ texture ⇒ 3.4 (ii) ⇒ committed `salt_spray`). „Glaze", „Topcoat" and „Gloss" are shine job nouns (with the R2-Q3 list: Glanz, Shine, Gloss, Finish) ⇒ `syoss-glaze-topcoat` („Glaze Topcoat": one job, shine; R3-Q3 lets the one-job name win) ⇒ `styling_result` ⇒ 3.5 ⇒ committed `shine_finish`. Slogans in a name („Big Hair Day", „Salon Blow-Out") name no job and are skipped (RG2-17). **Shop-title fallback `[R3-Q2]`:** the confirmed name is the pack name (C1) or the brand's German-page name (C2). When **neither** shows the product name, the **product-type noun of the retailer's product title** (Hitzeschutzspray, Öl, Serum, Haarspray, Gel, Wachs …; dm „syoss **Hitzeschutzspray** Keratin") serves as the confirmed-name job word for this step and for D2 (§4.3 3.1), with review `name_from_retailer_title`, **provided the type noun agrees across the retailer titles captured `[R3-H4 (d)]`** — two titles with different type nouns (e.g. „Hitzeschutzspray" vs „Haarspray") give no fallback: the name decides nothing, the lead falls to steps 2–3, review `retailer_title_type_noun_conflict` (R1-H1's two-job-word rule covers two nouns in **one** name). **Every other word of a retailer title never counts** (R2-H1, the C3 rule): qualifiers, variant names, ingredient words and any second noun stay C3 traces. The real pack names of the products concerned are captured (29 confirmed names were retailer-title only in round 3, node, `round-3/diff.json` `packet_checks.confirmed_name_tier_C3`; P3-7, R3-T), and a captured pack or brand-page name replaces the fallback (the round-4 freeze replaces it from `capture/packnames-r7.json` wherever A3/A11 confirm a name, §4.6). Cases: `syoss-hitzeschutzspray-keratin-heat` ⇒ heat protection ⇒ 3.3 (§11.21); `loreal-elvital-haaroel-oel-magique-alle-haartypen`, `john-frieda-haarserum-frizz-ease-der-baendiger`, `garnier-fructis-sleek-and-stay-heat-activated-serum` ⇒ „Öl"/„Serum" ⇒ D2 by the letter (§4.6);

| Decision | Structured judgment: primary = the job the C1/C2 lead promise (§4.2 order) states; secondaries = up to two further jobs the C1/C2 claims state explicitly. **Primary `[RG-11]`:** the first **job-bearing** phrase of the lead promise; product nouns (Gel, Gelee, Paste, Wachs) and strength phrases („mit mittlerem Halt") are not job-bearing unless nothing else is; shaping/forming wording maps to `hold_fix`. **A strength phrase is not job-bearing when it qualifies a product noun or follows another job phrase („Gel mit mittlerem Halt"); when the hold is the lead's subject („Intensiver Halt für …", „Starker Halt –") the lead states `hold_fix` `[RG2-4]`** (`syoss-professional-performance-max-hold-power-wax`: „Intensiver Halt für glatte und glänzende … Looks" ⇒ `hold_fix`). **A curl/wave noun with a shaping or setting verb („Locken formen", „Curl Shaper", „Wellen über Nacht") states `definition`; shaping without a curl/wave noun stays `hold_fix` `[RG2-5]`** (`syoss-curl-cream-gel-3in1` „Locken zu formen und zu definieren" ⇒ `definition`). **Job vocabulary `[RG2-6, RG2-7; R6-T (3)]`:** Schwung, Sprungkraft, Spannkraft, Fülle ⇒ `volume`; **an adjective before a job phrase is not a separate job `[R7-Q1]`** (Wellaflex „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition`). (Elastizität is a flexibility word, §6.9, never a job); taming or smoothing flyaways, „abstehende Haare/Härchen" or „Babyhaare" ⇒ `frizz_control`; `sleek` only for a smooth or straight result of the whole style („glatte Looks", „Sleek-Look") (`john-frieda-frizz-ease-zauberformel-seiden-finish-creme` „Glättet abstehende Haare" ⇒ `frizz_control`). **Definition `[R6-T (3), R7-Q2]`: a curl/wave word in the product's own confirmed name supplies `definition` (with §4.2's Beach Waves texture and curl-revival refresh exceptions); in descriptive sentences an explicit promise to define or shape curls/waves is required. „Definition“/„Define“ for a non-curl look and a result phrase such as „definierter Look“ never supply `definition`** (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance`: no definition secondary). **Secondaries `[RG-12; RG2-16, ruled „open" by R2-T]`:** any job word of this vocabulary stated in a C1/C2 promise line — including the RG-12 mappings: a C1/C2 hold claim with a strength word ⇒ `hold_fix`; an anti-frizz/flyaway word ⇒ `frizz_control`; a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; **job words of the confirmed name count as secondaries** after the primary, in name order, **before** the claim lines (still at most two). **Formula gate** (property set §2.12): `hold_fix` ⇒ the D8b hold-mechanism set (§7.5); `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. A failing secondary is **dropped and recorded**; a failing primary is **kept** and tagged `job_formula_conflict` + review. **Order, gate and refill `[RG4-17]`** (closes RG2-16's „open"): list the eligible candidates in order — the confirmed name's job words first (after the primary, in name order), then the C1/C2 promise lines in packet order, each line's job words in text order — and take the first two; apply the formula gate; when the gate drops one, **refill from the next eligible candidate** (still at most two). **Humidity and duration lines never state a job; an explicit anti-frizz word in them does** („Schutz vor Frizz & Feuchtigkeit" ⇒ `frizz_control`; „hält bis zu 72 h" ⇒ none). **A fixing verb without a strength word** („fixiert die Frisur zuverlässig") **states `hold_fix` as a secondary and sets no level `[RG4-12]`** (`balea-overnight-wellenspray`). **A technology, formula or complex label is never a job `[RG4-10]`** („POWER-SHINE-TECHNOLOGIE" states no `shine`). **Brand line / collection names never supply any job `[R7-Q3]`** (Frizz Ease, Traumlocken, Volume Lift, Diamond Sleek, Glow & Shine, Nutricurls …); the product's own name words decide (§4.2). **Names `[R4-Q2, R4-Q7, R7-Q2]`:** „Glaze", „Topcoat", „Gloss" state `shine`; „Beach Waves" / „Strandwellen" / „beachy" state `texture`; a product noun states `hold_fix` (molding/hold) and its shine or strength qualifier states no second job; a true job word beside it (Texture, Volume, Curl) is a job word (`got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay`: primary `hold_fix` from the lead C2 line, secondary `texture` from the name) |

name.confirmed_name: Styling Powder

directions.text: Eine kleine Menge Puder in den Handflächen verteilen und in das trockene Haar einarbeiten. Für maximales Volumen das Puder direkt am Haaransatz einmassieren und nach Wunsch stylen.

s0_promises.text: Das Balea MEN Styling Powder verleiht dem Haar Volumen und einen [CLAIM] Effekt. Es sorgt für extra Fülle und Textur, ideal für ein perfektes Ansatzvolumen und voluminöse Looks. Die leichte Formel hinterlässt ein [CLAIM] Finish ohne sichtbare Rückstände und beschwert das Haar nicht. Für ein individuelles und [CLAIM] Styling kann das Styling Powder einfach im trockenen Haar verteilt und nach Wunsch modelliert werden.

claims.text: Das Balea MEN Styling Powder verleiht dem Haar Volumen und einen matten Effekt. Es sorgt für extra Fülle und Textur, ideal für ein perfektes Ansatzvolumen und voluminöse Looks. Die leichte Formel hinterlässt ein mattes Finish ohne sichtbare Rückstände und beschwert das Haar nicht. Für ein individuelles und flexibles Styling kann das Styling Powder einfach im trockenen Haar verteilt und nach Wunsch modelliert werden.

rules.quote: 1. the **job word of the confirmed product name**, when it names exactly one (Lockencreme ⇒ definition; Hitzeschutzspray ⇒ heat protection; Finishing-Spray / Glanzspray ⇒ finish). **A name with two or more job words does not decide; go to step 2** `[R1-H1]` (Elnett „Stylingspray Hitzeschutz 3 Tage Glatt" ⇒ pack front „Hitze Styling-Spray, glatt 3 Tage, starker Halt" ⇒ styling result, as PH1-14 rules). **Counting the name's job words `[RG2-21, RG2-5]`:** the product-type noun (Haarspray, Gel, Wachs, Puder, Schaumfestiger) names the job when it is the only job noun, and a shine or strength qualifier in the same name is not a second job (`schwarzkopf-taft-haarspray-glanz-halt-4` „Haarspray Glanz Halt 4" ⇒ one job, hold, so `hairspray`, as §5 says); name job words that name the same job count as one (Curl + Defining + Shaper on a curl product; „Glanz-Spray … Silky Shine"). **Which name words are job words `[RG3-1]`:** a **curl or wave word** in the product's own name (Locken-, Curl, Curls, Wellen-, Wave/Waves) is a curl job word `[R7-Q2]` — definition, or refresh when the product revives curls; a **salt noun** (Salzspray, Sea Salt Spray) names texture; a **product noun used as a form in a compound with another product noun** (Wax Spray, Spray Wax, Sprühwachs, Gel-Spray) names the form, not a job — go to step 2/3. Round-3 outcomes (historical, subject to the R7 amendment above): `bali-curls-volumizing-curl-spray-refreshing` („Volumizing Curl Spray": two job words ⇒ first C2 line, revival ⇒ held `refresher`); `wellaflex-schaumfestiger-locken-und-wellen-starker-halt` (name has hold + definition; the C1 phrase „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition` under R7-Q1 ⇒ 3.4 (iii)); `kevin-murphy-killer-curls` (two job words ⇒ the C2 hold line leads ⇒ primary `hold_fix`; the route stays D7 `curl_cream`, held); `jean-und-len-sea-salt-spray` (salt noun ⇒ texture); `redken-wax-spray` (Wax Spray names the form ⇒ first C2 line „Texturierendes Sprühwachs" ⇒ texture ⇒ `texture_spray`, §5). **Product noun vs qualifier, also inside a compound `[R4-Q7]`:** a product-type noun in the name (Wachs/Wax, Paste, Clay, Gel, Pomade, Fiber, Haarspray) names the job (molding or hold); a **shine or strength qualifier** in the name (Glanz, Glow, Shine, Strong, Power) is the finish or the grade, **never a second job — also inside a compound** (as „Haarspray Glanz"). Two product nouns of the same job count once. A **true job word** beside the product noun (Texture, Volume, Curl) makes two jobs ⇒ the name decides nothing ⇒ the lead line decides (step 2/3). The RG3-1 form compound stays for a product noun joined with a dispensing-form noun (Wax Spray, Sprühwachs, Gel-Spray: the spray is the form). Cases: `schwarzkopf-taft-gel-wax-glanz-halt-2` („Gel Wax Glanz": Gel and Wax name one job, Glanz is the finish) ⇒ `molding`, primary `hold_fix`, finish `glänzend`, and its D8b flag is kept internally (R4-Q7; §7.5); `got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay` („Styling Paste … Texture Clay": Paste/Clay + the job word Texture ⇒ two jobs) ⇒ the C2 line „… ultra krassem Halt" leads ⇒ primary `hold_fix`, `texture` secondary; `balea-haarwachs-glow-wax` (Glow is a qualifier) ⇒ `hold_fix`. **Look names and shine nouns `[R4-Q2]`:** „Beach Waves", „Strandwellen", „beachy" name the **salt-spray texture look** ⇒ `texture` (`li_function: no`), not curl definition; RG3-1's wave nouns cover curl/wave definition and revival products („Wellen-Spray", „Wellenauffrischer"), not beach-look names (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance` ⇒ texture ⇒ 3.4 (ii) ⇒ committed `salt_spray`). „Glaze", „Topcoat" and „Gloss" are shine job nouns (with the R2-Q3 list: Glanz, Shine, Gloss, Finish) ⇒ `syoss-glaze-topcoat` („Glaze Topcoat": one job, shine; R3-Q3 lets the one-job name win) ⇒ `styling_result` ⇒ 3.5 ⇒ committed `shine_finish`. Slogans in a name („Big Hair Day", „Salon Blow-Out") name no job and are skipped (RG2-17). **Shop-title fallback `[R3-Q2]`:** the confirmed name is the pack name (C1) or the brand's German-page name (C2). When **neither** shows the product name, the **product-type noun of the retailer's product title** (Hitzeschutzspray, Öl, Serum, Haarspray, Gel, Wachs …; dm „syoss **Hitzeschutzspray** Keratin") serves as the confirmed-name job word for this step and for D2 (§4.3 3.1), with review `name_from_retailer_title`, **provided the type noun agrees across the retailer titles captured `[R3-H4 (d)]`** — two titles with different type nouns (e.g. „Hitzeschutzspray" vs „Haarspray") give no fallback: the name decides nothing, the lead falls to steps 2–3, review `retailer_title_type_noun_conflict` (R1-H1's two-job-word rule covers two nouns in **one** name). **Every other word of a retailer title never counts** (R2-H1, the C3 rule): qualifiers, variant names, ingredient words and any second noun stay C3 traces. The real pack names of the products concerned are captured (29 confirmed names were retailer-title only in round 3, node, `round-3/diff.json` `packet_checks.confirmed_name_tier_C3`; P3-7, R3-T), and a captured pack or brand-page name replaces the fallback (the round-4 freeze replaces it from `capture/packnames-r7.json` wherever A3/A11 confirm a name, §4.6). Cases: `syoss-hitzeschutzspray-keratin-heat` ⇒ heat protection ⇒ 3.3 (§11.21); `loreal-elvital-haaroel-oel-magique-alle-haartypen`, `john-frieda-haarserum-frizz-ease-der-baendiger`, `garnier-fructis-sleek-and-stay-heat-activated-serum` ⇒ „Öl"/„Serum" ⇒ D2 by the letter (§4.6);

| Decision | Structured judgment: primary = the job the C1/C2 lead promise (§4.2 order) states; secondaries = up to two further jobs the C1/C2 claims state explicitly. **Primary `[RG-11]`:** the first **job-bearing** phrase of the lead promise; product nouns (Gel, Gelee, Paste, Wachs) and strength phrases („mit mittlerem Halt") are not job-bearing unless nothing else is; shaping/forming wording maps to `hold_fix`. **A strength phrase is not job-bearing when it qualifies a product noun or follows another job phrase („Gel mit mittlerem Halt"); when the hold is the lead's subject („Intensiver Halt für …", „Starker Halt –") the lead states `hold_fix` `[RG2-4]`** (`syoss-professional-performance-max-hold-power-wax`: „Intensiver Halt für glatte und glänzende … Looks" ⇒ `hold_fix`). **A curl/wave noun with a shaping or setting verb („Locken formen", „Curl Shaper", „Wellen über Nacht") states `definition`; shaping without a curl/wave noun stays `hold_fix` `[RG2-5]`** (`syoss-curl-cream-gel-3in1` „Locken zu formen und zu definieren" ⇒ `definition`). **Job vocabulary `[RG2-6, RG2-7; R6-T (3)]`:** Schwung, Sprungkraft, Spannkraft, Fülle ⇒ `volume`; **an adjective before a job phrase is not a separate job `[R7-Q1]`** (Wellaflex „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition`). (Elastizität is a flexibility word, §6.9, never a job); taming or smoothing flyaways, „abstehende Haare/Härchen" or „Babyhaare" ⇒ `frizz_control`; `sleek` only for a smooth or straight result of the whole style („glatte Looks", „Sleek-Look") (`john-frieda-frizz-ease-zauberformel-seiden-finish-creme` „Glättet abstehende Haare" ⇒ `frizz_control`). **Definition `[R6-T (3), R7-Q2]`: a curl/wave word in the product's own confirmed name supplies `definition` (with §4.2's Beach Waves texture and curl-revival refresh exceptions); in descriptive sentences an explicit promise to define or shape curls/waves is required. „Definition“/„Define“ for a non-curl look and a result phrase such as „definierter Look“ never supply `definition`** (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance`: no definition secondary). **Secondaries `[RG-12; RG2-16, ruled „open" by R2-T]`:** any job word of this vocabulary stated in a C1/C2 promise line — including the RG-12 mappings: a C1/C2 hold claim with a strength word ⇒ `hold_fix`; an anti-frizz/flyaway word ⇒ `frizz_control`; a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; **job words of the confirmed name count as secondaries** after the primary, in name order, **before** the claim lines (still at most two). **Formula gate** (property set §2.12): `hold_fix` ⇒ the D8b hold-mechanism set (§7.5); `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. A failing secondary is **dropped and recorded**; a failing primary is **kept** and tagged `job_formula_conflict` + review. **Order, gate and refill `[RG4-17]`** (closes RG2-16's „open"): list the eligible candidates in order — the confirmed name's job words first (after the primary, in name order), then the C1/C2 promise lines in packet order, each line's job words in text order — and take the first two; apply the formula gate; when the gate drops one, **refill from the next eligible candidate** (still at most two). **Humidity and duration lines never state a job; an explicit anti-frizz word in them does** („Schutz vor Frizz & Feuchtigkeit" ⇒ `frizz_control`; „hält bis zu 72 h" ⇒ none). **A fixing verb without a strength word** („fixiert die Frisur zuverlässig") **states `hold_fix` as a secondary and sets no level `[RG4-12]`** (`balea-overnight-wellenspray`). **A technology, formula or complex label is never a job `[RG4-10]`** („POWER-SHINE-TECHNOLOGIE" states no `shine`). **Brand line / collection names never supply any job `[R7-Q3]`** (Frizz Ease, Traumlocken, Volume Lift, Diamond Sleek, Glow & Shine, Nutricurls …); the product's own name words decide (§4.2). **Names `[R4-Q2, R4-Q7, R7-Q2]`:** „Glaze", „Topcoat", „Gloss" state `shine`; „Beach Waves" / „Strandwellen" / „beachy" state `texture`; a product noun states `hold_fix` (molding/hold) and its shine or strength qualifier states no second job; a true job word beside it (Texture, Volume, Curl) is a job word (`got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay`: primary `hold_fix` from the lead C2 line, secondary `texture` from the name) |

lane_errors.explanation: §4.2 explicitly includes Puder as a job-bearing product-type noun; §6.10 maps a product noun to hold_fix. The short illustrative molding-noun list is not an exception to this generic rule. Styling Powder therefore supplies a vocabulary job and R7-F cannot skip it. B hold_fix is primary; the C2 promise supplies volume then texture, both passing particulate/natural_film gates. A incorrectly falls through to the later volume promise and moves the real primary hold_fix into secondary jobs.

Slogans in a name („Big Hair Day", „Salon Blow-Out") name no job and are skipped (RG2-17). **Shop-title fallback `[R3-Q2]`:** the confirmed name is the pack name (C1) or the brand's German-page name (C2). When **neither** shows the product name, the **product-type noun of the retailer's product title** (Hitzeschutzspray, Öl, Serum, Haarspray, Gel, Wachs …; dm „syoss **Hitzeschutzspray** Keratin") serves as the confirmed-name job word for this step and for D2 (§4.3 3.1), with review `name_from_retailer_title`, **provided the type noun agrees across the retailer titles captured `[R3-H4 (d)]`** — two titles with different type nouns (e.g. „Hitzeschutzspray" vs „Haarspray") give no fallback: the name decides nothing, the lead falls to steps 2–3, review `retailer_title_type_noun_conflict` (R1-H1's two-job-word rule covers two nouns in **one** name). **Every other word of a retailer title never counts** (R2-H1, the C3 rule): qualifiers, variant names, ingredient words and any second noun stay C3 traces. rules.quote: | Decision | Structured judgment: primary = the job the C1/C2 lead promise (§4.2 order) states; secondaries = up to two further jobs the C1/C2 claims state explicitly. **Primary `[RG-11]`:** the first **job-bearing** phrase of the lead promise; product nouns (Gel, Gelee, Paste, Wachs) and strength phrases („mit mittlerem Halt") are not job-bearing unless nothing else is; shaping/forming wording maps to `hold_fix`. **A strength phrase is not job-bearing when it qualifies a product noun or follows another job phrase („Gel mit mittlerem Halt"); when the hold is the lead's subject („Intensiver Halt für …", „Starker Halt –") the lead states `hold_fix` `[RG2-4]`** (`syoss-professional-performance-max-hold-power-wax`: „Intensiver Halt für glatte und glänzende … Looks" ⇒ `hold_fix`). **A curl/wave noun with a shaping or setting verb („Locken formen", „Curl Shaper", „Wellen über Nacht") states `definition`; shaping without a curl/wave noun stays `hold_fix` `[RG2-5]`** (`syoss-curl-cream-gel-3in1` „Locken zu formen und zu definieren" ⇒ `definition`). **Job vocabulary `[RG2-6, RG2-7; R6-T (3)]`:** Schwung, Sprungkraft, Spannkraft, Fülle ⇒ `volume`; **an adjective before a job phrase is not a separate job `[R7-Q1]`** (Wellaflex „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition`). (Elastizität is a flexibility word, §6.9, never a job); taming or smoothing flyaways, „abstehende Haare/Härchen" or „Babyhaare" ⇒ `frizz_control`; `sleek` only for a smooth or straight result of the whole style („glatte Looks", „Sleek-Look") (`john-frieda-frizz-ease-zauberformel-seiden-finish-creme` „Glättet abstehende Haare" ⇒ `frizz_control`). **Definition `[R6-T (3), R7-Q2]`: a curl/wave word in the product's own confirmed name supplies `definition` (with §4.2's Beach Waves texture and curl-revival refresh exceptions); in descriptive sentences an explicit promise to define or shape curls/waves is required. „Definition“/„Define“ for a non-curl look and a result phrase such as „definierter Look“ never supply `definition`** (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance`: no definition secondary). **Secondaries `[RG-12; RG2-16, ruled „open" by R2-T]`:** any job word of this vocabulary stated in a C1/C2 promise line — including the RG-12 mappings: a C1/C2 hold claim with a strength word ⇒ `hold_fix`; an anti-frizz/flyaway word ⇒ `frizz_control`; a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; **job words of the confirmed name count as secondaries** after the primary, in name order, **before** the claim lines (still at most two). **Formula gate** (property set §2.12): `hold_fix` ⇒ the D8b hold-mechanism set (§7.5); `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. A failing secondary is **dropped and recorded**; a failing primary is **kept** and tagged `job_formula_conflict` + review. **Order, gate and refill `[RG4-17]`** (closes RG2-16's „open"): list the eligible candidates in order — the confirmed name's job words first (after the primary, in name order), then the C1/C2 promise lines in packet order, each line's job words in text order — and take the first two; apply the formula gate; when the gate drops one, **refill from the next eligible candidate** (still at most two). **Humidity and duration lines never state a job; an explicit anti-frizz word in them does** („Schutz vor Frizz & Feuchtigkeit" ⇒ `frizz_control`; „hält bis zu 72 h" ⇒ none). **A fixing verb without a strength word** („fixiert die Frisur zuverlässig") **states `hold_fix` as a secondary and sets no level `[RG4-12]`** (`balea-overnight-wellenspray`). **A technology, formula or complex label is never a job `[RG4-10]`** („POWER-SHINE-TECHNOLOGIE" states no `shine`). **Brand line / collection names never supply any job `[R7-Q3]`** (Frizz Ease, Traumlocken, Volume Lift, Diamond Sleek, Glow & Shine, Nutricurls …); the product's own name words decide (§4.2). **Names `[R4-Q2, R4-Q7, R7-Q2]`:** „Glaze", „Topcoat", „Gloss" state `shine`; „Beach Waves" / „Strandwellen" / „beachy" state `texture`; a product noun states `hold_fix` (molding/hold) and its shine or strength qualifier states no second job; a true job word beside it (Texture, Volume, Curl) is a job word (`got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay`: primary `hold_fix` from the lead C2 line, secondary `texture` from the name) |
