rules.quote: | Decision | Structured judgment: primary = the job the C1/C2 lead promise (§4.2 order) states; secondaries = up to two further jobs the C1/C2 claims state explicitly. **Primary `[RG-11]`:** the first **job-bearing** phrase of the lead promise; product nouns (Gel, Gelee, Paste, Wachs) and strength phrases („mit mittlerem Halt") are not job-bearing unless nothing else is; shaping/forming wording maps to `hold_fix`. **A strength phrase is not job-bearing when it qualifies a product noun or follows another job phrase („Gel mit mittlerem Halt"); when the hold is the lead's subject („Intensiver Halt für …", „Starker Halt –") the lead states `hold_fix` `[RG2-4]`** (`syoss-professional-performance-max-hold-power-wax`: „Intensiver Halt für glatte und glänzende … Looks" ⇒ `hold_fix`). **A curl/wave noun with a shaping or setting verb („Locken formen", „Curl Shaper", „Wellen über Nacht") states `definition`; shaping without a curl/wave noun stays `hold_fix` `[RG2-5]`** (`syoss-curl-cream-gel-3in1` „Locken zu formen und zu definieren" ⇒ `definition`). **Job vocabulary `[RG2-6, RG2-7; R6-T (3)]`:** Schwung, Sprungkraft, Spannkraft, Fülle ⇒ `volume`; **an adjective before a job phrase is not a separate job `[R7-Q1]`** (Wellaflex „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition`). (Elastizität is a flexibility word, §6.9, never a job); taming or smoothing flyaways, „abstehende Haare/Härchen" or „Babyhaare" ⇒ `frizz_control`; `sleek` only for a smooth or straight result of the whole style („glatte Looks", „Sleek-Look") (`john-frieda-frizz-ease-zauberformel-seiden-finish-creme` „Glättet abstehende Haare" ⇒ `frizz_control`). **Definition `[R6-T (3), R7-Q2]`: a curl/wave word in the product's own confirmed name supplies `definition` (with §4.2's Beach Waves texture and curl-revival refresh exceptions); in descriptive sentences an explicit promise to define or shape curls/waves is required. „Definition“/„Define“ for a non-curl look and a result phrase such as „definierter Look“ never supply `definition`** (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance`: no definition secondary). **Secondaries `[RG-12; RG2-16, ruled „open" by R2-T]`:** any job word of this vocabulary stated in a C1/C2 promise line — including the RG-12 mappings: a C1/C2 hold claim with a strength word ⇒ `hold_fix`; an anti-frizz/flyaway word ⇒ `frizz_control`; a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. rules.quote: | Decision | Transcription against the property-set anchors (§2.13), from the verbatim directions (any G1 tier; not claim-gated). **Reading the two damp anchors `[operational — property set §2.13 anchor text]`:** `before_heat` when the directions make a heat step a **required** next step (blow-dry or iron named, no air-dry option) or apply to dry hair before a hot tool; `damp_before_drying` when air-drying is allowed, drying is unspecified, or blow-drying is offered as optional („für optimales Ergebnis föhnen"). This resolves property set §9 item 4: `alcina-foehn-lotion` and `balea-foehnlotion-volume-effect` both read `before_heat` if their directions require the blow-dry. `second_day` only when the **directions** lead with refreshing between washes — marketing copy („ideal zum Auffrischen") is not directions. **Spray-only directions `[RG-2]`:** directions that consist only of spraying the product onto the hair (distance, evenness, optional targeting of strands — „Aus 30 cm Abstand sprühen") with no moisture state, no drying or heat step and no shaping step read **`dry_finish`** (the product is applied last, onto the finished style), confidence `moderate`; missing or copied directions stay `unresolved`. **Equal alternatives `[RG-8]`:** when the directions offer two moments as equal options („in handtuchtrockenes oder trockenes Haar", „feucht oder trocken"), the **first-named** is primary and the others go to `also[]`. **`dry_restyle` needs a named shaping act `[RG2-8]`** (kneten, einkneten, formen, stylen, in Form bringen, toupieren; **also einarbeiten, durcharbeiten, mit den Fingern verteilen und formen `[RG3-7]`**; and **a paste, wax, cream or powder worked into dry hair by hand is `dry_restyle` `[RG3-7]`** — `got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay` „zwischen deinen Handflächen [verreiben] und … ins trockene Haar ein[arbeiten]", `osis-dust-it` „mit den Fingern in das trockene Haar einarbeiten", `syoss-professional-performance-max-hold-power-wax` „in den Handflächen verreiben … Auf trockenem Haar anwenden"): spraying or distributing on dry hair without one is `dry_finish`; a product sprayed strand by strand to revive curls is `dry_finish` (`alverde-locken-refresh-spray`), while a named shaping act such as „und nach Wunsch stylen" or „einkneten" makes it `dry_restyle` (`redken-refreshing-curl-mist` „sprühen und sanft einkneten" ⇒ `dry_restyle`). **Shaping with no moisture state `[RG2-9]`** (mirror of RG-2): directions that name a shaping step but no moisture state, no drying and no heat step read **`dry_restyle`**, confidence `moderate` (`redken-powder-grip-03` „über das Haar streuen … mit den Fingern durch das Haar kneten"; `redken-root-tease`; `got2b-kleber-4-brows-and-edges-2in1-stylinggel`); missing or copied directions stay `unresolved`. **Stroking over dry hair without a shaping act `[RG4-14]`** (a stick passed over the finished style to lay down flyaways) is `dry_finish` (`balea-styling-finishing-stick` „Nach dem Frisurenstyling sanft über die abstehenden Härchen streichen") |

rules.quote: 1. the **job word of the confirmed product name**, when it names exactly one (Lockencreme ⇒ definition; Hitzeschutzspray ⇒ heat protection; Finishing-Spray / Glanzspray ⇒ finish). **A name with two or more job words does not decide; go to step 2** `[R1-H1]` (Elnett „Stylingspray Hitzeschutz 3 Tage Glatt" ⇒ pack front „Hitze Styling-Spray, glatt 3 Tage, starker Halt" ⇒ styling result, as PH1-14 rules). **Counting the name's job words `[RG2-21, RG2-5]`:** the product-type noun (Haarspray, Gel, Wachs, Puder, Schaumfestiger) names the job when it is the only job noun, and a shine or strength qualifier in the same name is not a second job (`schwarzkopf-taft-haarspray-glanz-halt-4` „Haarspray Glanz Halt 4" ⇒ one job, hold, so `hairspray`, as §5 says); name job words that name the same job count as one (Curl + Defining + Shaper on a curl product; „Glanz-Spray … Silky Shine"). **Which name words are job words `[RG3-1]`:** a **curl or wave word** in the product's own name (Locken-, Curl, Curls, Wellen-, Wave/Waves) is a curl job word `[R7-Q2]` — definition, or refresh when the product revives curls; a **salt noun** (Salzspray, Sea Salt Spray) names texture; a **product noun used as a form in a compound with another product noun** (Wax Spray, Spray Wax, Sprühwachs, Gel-Spray) names the form, not a job — go to step 2/3. Round-3 outcomes (historical, subject to the R7 amendment above): `bali-curls-volumizing-curl-spray-refreshing` („Volumizing Curl Spray": two job words ⇒ first C2 line, revival ⇒ held `refresher`); `wellaflex-schaumfestiger-locken-und-wellen-starker-halt` (name has hold + definition; the C1 phrase „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition` under R7-Q1 ⇒ 3.4 (iii)); `kevin-murphy-killer-curls` (two job words ⇒ the C2 hold line leads ⇒ primary `hold_fix`; the route stays D7 `curl_cream`, held); `jean-und-len-sea-salt-spray` (salt noun ⇒ texture); `redken-wax-spray` (Wax Spray names the form ⇒ first C2 line „Texturierendes Sprühwachs" ⇒ texture ⇒ `texture_spray`, §5). **Product noun vs qualifier, also inside a compound `[R4-Q7]`:** a product-type noun in the name (Wachs/Wax, Paste, Clay, Gel, Pomade, Fiber, Haarspray) names the job (molding or hold); a **shine or strength qualifier** in the name (Glanz, Glow, Shine, Strong, Power) is the finish or the grade, **never a second job — also inside a compound** (as „Haarspray Glanz"). Two product nouns of the same job count once. A **true job word** beside the product noun (Texture, Volume, Curl) makes two jobs ⇒ the name decides nothing ⇒ the lead line decides (step 2/3). The RG3-1 form compound stays for a product noun joined with a dispensing-form noun (Wax Spray, Sprühwachs, Gel-Spray: the spray is the form). Cases: `schwarzkopf-taft-gel-wax-glanz-halt-2` („Gel Wax Glanz": Gel and Wax name one job, Glanz is the finish) ⇒ `molding`, primary `hold_fix`, finish `glänzend`, and its D8b flag is kept internally (R4-Q7; §7.5); `got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay` („Styling Paste … Texture Clay": Paste/Clay + the job word Texture ⇒ two jobs) ⇒ the C2 line „… ultra krassem Halt" leads ⇒ primary `hold_fix`, `texture` secondary; `balea-haarwachs-glow-wax` (Glow is a qualifier) ⇒ `hold_fix`. **Look names and shine nouns `[R4-Q2]`:** „Beach Waves", „Strandwellen", „beachy" name the **salt-spray texture look** ⇒ `texture` (`li_function: no`), not curl definition; RG3-1's wave nouns cover curl/wave definition and revival products („Wellen-Spray", „Wellenauffrischer"), not beach-look names (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance` ⇒ texture ⇒ 3.4 (ii) ⇒ committed `salt_spray`). „Glaze", „Topcoat" and „Gloss" are shine job nouns (with the R2-Q3 list: Glanz, Shine, Gloss, Finish) ⇒ `syoss-glaze-topcoat` („Glaze Topcoat": one job, shine; R3-Q3 lets the one-job name win) ⇒ `styling_result` ⇒ 3.5 ⇒ committed `shine_finish`. Slogans in a name („Big Hair Day", „Salon Blow-Out") name no job and are skipped (RG2-17). **Shop-title fallback `[R3-Q2]`:** the confirmed name is the pack name (C1) or the brand's German-page name (C2). When **neither** shows the product name, the **product-type noun of the retailer's product title** (Hitzeschutzspray, Öl, Serum, Haarspray, Gel, Wachs …; dm „syoss **Hitzeschutzspray** Keratin") serves as the confirmed-name job word for this step and for D2 (§4.3 3.1), with review `name_from_retailer_title`, **provided the type noun agrees across the retailer titles captured `[R3-H4 (d)]`** — two titles with different type nouns (e.g. „Hitzeschutzspray" vs „Haarspray") give no fallback: the name decides nothing, the lead falls to steps 2–3, review `retailer_title_type_noun_conflict` (R1-H1's two-job-word rule covers two nouns in **one** name). **Every other word of a retailer title never counts** (R2-H1, the C3 rule): qualifiers, variant names, ingredient words and any second noun stay C3 traces. The real pack names of the products concerned are captured (29 confirmed names were retailer-title only in round 3, node, `round-3/diff.json` `packet_checks.confirmed_name_tier_C3`; P3-7, R3-T), and a captured pack or brand-page name replaces the fallback (the round-4 freeze replaces it from `capture/packnames-r7.json` wherever A3/A11 confirm a name, §4.6). (Elastizität is a flexibility word, §6.9, never a job); taming or smoothing flyaways, „abstehende Haare/Härchen" or „Babyhaare" ⇒ `frizz_control`; `sleek` only for a smooth or straight result of the whole style („glatte Looks", „Sleek-Look") (`john-frieda-frizz-ease-zauberformel-seiden-finish-creme` „Glättet abstehende Haare" ⇒ `frizz_control`). **Definition `[R6-T (3), R7-Q2]`: a curl/wave word in the product's own confirmed name supplies `definition` (with §4.2's Beach Waves texture and curl-revival refresh exceptions); in descriptive sentences an explicit promise to define or shape curls/waves is required. „Definition“/„Define“ for a non-curl look and a result phrase such as „definierter Look“ never supply `definition`** (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance`: no definition secondary). **Secondaries `[RG-12; RG2-16, ruled „open" by R2-T]`:** any job word of this vocabulary stated in a C1/C2 promise line — including the RG-12 mappings: a C1/C2 hold claim with a strength word ⇒ `hold_fix`; an anti-frizz/flyaway word ⇒ `frizz_control`; a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; **job words of the confirmed name count as secondaries** after the primary, in name order, **before** the claim lines (still at most two). **Formula gate** (property set §2.12): `hold_fix` ⇒ the D8b hold-mechanism set (§7.5); `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. A failing secondary is **dropped and recorded**; a failing primary is **kept** and tagged `job_formula_conflict` + review. **Order, gate and refill `[RG4-17]`** (closes RG2-16's „open"): list the eligible candidates in order — the confirmed name's job words first (after the primary, in name order), then the C1/C2 promise lines in packet order, each line's job words in text order — and take the first two; apply the formula gate; when the gate drops one, **refill from the next eligible candidate** (still at most two). **Humidity and duration lines never state a job; an explicit anti-frizz word in them does** („Schutz vor Frizz & Feuchtigkeit" ⇒ `frizz_control`; „hält bis zu 72 h" ⇒ none). **A fixing verb without a strength word** („fixiert die Frisur zuverlässig") **states `hold_fix` as a secondary and sets no level `[RG4-12]`** (`balea-overnight-wellenspray`). **A technology, formula or complex label is never a job `[RG4-10]`** („POWER-SHINE-TECHNOLOGIE" states no `shine`). **Brand line / collection names never supply any job `[R7-Q3]`** (Frizz Ease, Traumlocken, Volume Lift, Diamond Sleek, Glow & Shine, Nutricurls …); the product's own name words decide (§4.2). **Names `[R4-Q2, R4-Q7, R7-Q2]`:** „Glaze", „Topcoat", „Gloss" state `shine`; „Beach Waves" / „Strandwellen" / „beachy" state `texture`; a product noun states `hold_fix` (molding/hold) and its shine or strength qualifier states no second job; a true job word beside it (Texture, Volume, Curl) is a job word (`got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay`: primary `hold_fix` from the lead C2 line, secondary `texture` from the name) |

| Decision | Transcription against the property-set anchors (§2.13), from the verbatim directions (any G1 tier; not claim-gated). **Reading the two damp anchors `[operational — property set §2.13 anchor text]`:** `before_heat` when the directions make a heat step a **required** next step (blow-dry or iron named, no air-dry option) or apply to dry hair before a hot tool; `damp_before_drying` when air-drying is allowed, drying is unspecified, or blow-drying is offered as optional („für optimales Ergebnis föhnen"). rules.quote: | R7-Q1 | **An adjective in front of a job phrase is not its own job** (owner): Wellaflex Schaumfestiger Locken & Wellen „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken" ⇒ primary `definition`. |

rules.matched_fragment: the first **job-bearing** phrase of the lead promise
rules.quote: | Decision | Structured judgment: primary = the job the C1/C2 lead promise (§4.2 order) states; secondaries = up to two further jobs the C1/C2 claims state explicitly. **Primary `[RG-11]`:** the first **job-bearing** phrase of the lead promise; product nouns (Gel, Gelee, Paste, Wachs) and strength phrases („mit mittlerem Halt") are not job-bearing unless nothing else is; shaping/forming wording maps to `hold_fix`. **A strength phrase is not job-bearing when it qualifies a product noun or follows another job phrase („Gel mit mittlerem Halt"); when the hold is the lead's subject („Intensiver Halt für …", „Starker Halt –") the lead states `hold_fix` `[RG2-4]`** (`syoss-professional-performance-max-hold-power-wax`: „Intensiver Halt für glatte und glänzende … Looks" ⇒ `hold_fix`). **A curl/wave noun with a shaping or setting verb („Locken formen", „Curl Shaper", „Wellen über Nacht") states `definition`; shaping without a curl/wave noun stays `hold_fix` `[RG2-5]`** (`syoss-curl-cream-gel-3in1` „Locken zu formen und zu definieren" ⇒ `definition`). **Job vocabulary `[RG2-6, RG2-7; R6-T (3)]`:** Schwung, Sprungkraft, Spannkraft, Fülle ⇒ `volume`; **an adjective before a job phrase is not a separate job `[R7-Q1]`** (Wellaflex „für schwungvolle, definierte Locken“ ⇒ primary `definition`). (Elastizität is a flexibility word, §6.9, never a job); taming or smoothing flyaways, „abstehende Haare/Härchen" or „Babyhaare" ⇒ `frizz_control`; `sleek` only for a smooth or straight result of the whole style („glatte Looks", „Sleek-Look") (`john-frieda-frizz-ease-zauberformel-seiden-finish-creme` „Glättet abstehende Haare" ⇒ `frizz_control`). **Definition `[R6-T (3), R7-Q2]`: a curl/wave word in the product's own confirmed name supplies `definition` (with §4.2's Beach Waves texture and curl-revival refresh exceptions); in descriptive sentences an explicit promise to define or shape curls/waves is required. „Definition“/„Define“ for a non-curl look and a result phrase such as „definierter Look“ never supply `definition`** (`alverde-beach-waves-spray-seaside-balance`: no definition secondary). **Secondaries `[RG-12; RG2-16, ruled „open" by R2-T]`:** any job word of this vocabulary stated in a C1/C2 promise line — including the RG-12 mappings: a C1/C2 hold claim with a strength word ⇒ `hold_fix`; an anti-frizz/flyaway word ⇒ `frizz_control`; a shine word ⇒ `shine`; an explicit curl/wave definition promise ⇒ `definition` — and also volume, texture, sleek and refresh words; taken in claim order, at most two, after the primary; feel, ingredient and duration lines never state a job. **Masked or numeric hold claims and name job words `[RG3-16]`:** a hold claim with a strength word **or a brand number** states `hold_fix` — a masked strength in the blind packet („[CLAIM] Halt") or a bare Haltegrad still states the job, because the mask hides the grade, not the job; **job words of the confirmed name count as secondaries** after the primary, in name order, **before** the claim lines (still at most two). **Formula gate** (property set §2.12): `hold_fix` ⇒ the D8b hold-mechanism set (§7.5); `volume` ⇒ fixative_film / natural_film / particulate / salt; `texture` ⇒ particulate / salt / structuring wax_lipid / a film; `sleek` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / fixative_film; `shine` ⇒ wax_lipid / silicone_coat; `frizz_control` ⇒ silicone_coat / wax_lipid / a film; `definition` ⇒ any mechanism except humectant_only/none; `refresh` ⇒ any. A failing secondary is **dropped and recorded**; a failing primary is **kept** and tagged `job_formula_conflict` + review. **Order, gate and refill `[RG4-17]`** (closes RG2-16's „open"): list the eligible candidates in order — the confirmed name's job words first (after the primary, in name order), then the C1/C2 promise lines in packet order, each line's job words in text order — and take the first two; apply the formula gate; when the gate drops one, **refill from the next eligible candidate** (still at most two). **Humidity and duration lines never state a job; an explicit anti-frizz word in them does** („Schutz vor Frizz & Feuchtigkeit" ⇒ `frizz_control`; „hält bis zu 72 h" ⇒ none). **A fixing verb without a strength word** („fixiert die Frisur zuverlässig") **states `hold_fix` as a secondary and sets no level `[RG4-12]`** (`balea-overnight-wellenspray`). **A technology, formula or complex label is never a job `[RG4-10]`** („POWER-SHINE-TECHNOLOGIE" states no `shine`). **Brand line / collection names never supply any job `[R7-Q3]`** (Frizz Ease, Traumlocken, Volume Lift, Diamond Sleek, Glow & Shine, Nutricurls …); the product's own name words decide (§4.2). **Names `[R4-Q2, R4-Q7, R7-Q2]`:** „Glaze", „Topcoat", „Gloss" state `shine`; „Beach Waves" / „Strandwellen" / „beachy" state `texture`; a product noun states `hold_fix` (molding/hold) and its shine or strength qualifier states no second job; a true job word beside it (Texture, Volume, Curl) is a job word (`got2b-styling-paste-istyler-texture-clay`: primary `hold_fix` from the lead C2 line, secondary `texture` from the name) |

limitations: Targeted known-product confirmation; not a full new cohort, new unseen validation, catalog activation or live-app proof.
Human interpretation and proposed contract text are explicit. Joins, normalization, field/product counts, classifications tallies, ruling pass flags, hold counts, manifests and verdict are computed.
This scores lock readiness; it does not rewrite LOCK-1-S, owner approvals, frozen lane values or engine status.
Calculation-log differences and lane-reported latent ambiguities do not block. No subtype minimum or historical unseen gate is added to the user-specified targeted lock rule.

Agreement is not proof against shared mistakes. Named ruling effects are checked separately; hold_check is a raw A/B agreement check with frozen claim traces, not a newly implemented independent hold classifier.
